Aragonese

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • abre, arbre

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Latin arbor.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈaɾbol/
  • Syllabification: ár‧bol
  • Rhymes: -aɾbol

Noun

[edit]

árbol m

  1. tree

References

[edit]
  • “árbol”, in Aragonario, diccionario castellano–aragonés (in Spanish)
  • “árbol / abre, arbre”, in Diccionario ortografico de l’aragonés (seguntes la PO de l’EFA)‎[1], Zaragoza: EDACAR, 2023, →ISSN, page 202

Asturian

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • árbole, árbore

Etymology

[edit]

From Old Leonese arbol, from Latin arbor.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈaɾbol/ [ˈaɾ.β̞ol]
  • Rhymes: -aɾbol
  • Syllabification: ár‧bol

Noun

[edit]

árbol m (plural árboles)

  1. tree

Leonese

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • árbore

Etymology

[edit]

From Old Leonese arbol, from Latin arbor, arborem.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈaɾbol/, [ˈaɾ.β̞ol]
  • Hyphenation: ár‧bol

Noun

[edit]

árbol m (plural árboles)

  1. tree

References

  • “árbol”, in Diccionario Castellano-Leonés / Leonés-Castellano [Spanish-Leonese / Leonese-Spanish Dictionary] (in Spanish), La Asociación L'Alderique, 2012–2026
  • “árbol”, in Pallabreiru Llïonés [Leonese Dictionary] (in Spanish), 2026

Spanish

[edit]
Spanish Wikipedia has an article on:
árbol
Wikipedia es

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • árbor (obsolete)

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Spanish arbol, arbor, from Latin arborem f. Compare Portuguese árvore.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈaɾbol/ [ˈaɾ.β̞ol]
  • Audio (Spain):(file)
  • Audio (Peru):(file)
  • Rhymes: -aɾbol
  • Syllabification: ár‧bol

Noun

[edit]

árbol m (plural árboles)

  1. tree (a perennial woody plant)
  2. tree (any plant that is reminiscent of the above but not classified as a tree)
  3. tree (any structure or construct having branches representing divergence or possible choices)
  4. (nautical) mast (a tall, slim post or tower used to support the sails on a ship)
    Synonyms: mástil, palo
